sheet.summary: Caln Township's only audit in the 2023 to 2025 window is 2023, and it has one serious finding: a required federal report was not accurate or filed on time. The finding is not a repeat and has no questioned costs, so the rating is medium. No 2024 or 2025 audit is on file, so this picture may be out of date.

reasons.reason: The auditor marked this reporting failure as a material weakness (the most serious kind of control problem) and gave a modified opinion on compliance for the federal program, which makes it a serious finding in the latest audit on file.
reasons.quote: The Township did not properly complete and file the report on an accurate, timely basis.

next_checks: Confirm whether Caln Township was required to file single audits for 2024 and 2025, and if so why none is on file.
Ask the Township which report and federal program finding 2023-002 covers, and whether the report has since been corrected and filed.
The 2023 audit flags a material weakness and material noncompliance at the audit level; read the full 2023 audit report to see whether these go beyond finding 2023-002.

sheet.summary: Rated high. The latest audit on file (2024) found that a federally funded school construction contract again left out required wage-rate terms, which led the auditor to give a modified (not clean) opinion on compliance for the school relief programs, and the same problem was reported in 2023. The City also filed its audit form late in both years, and no 2025 audit is on file.

reasons.reason: The auditor treated the missing wage-rate terms as material noncompliance and gave a modified opinion on compliance for the school relief programs, which makes this a serious finding in the latest audit.
reasons.quote: the contract did not include the required Wage Rate (Davis Bacon Act) and DOL regulations.

reasons.reason: The serious finding is a repeat of the prior year's finding, which meets the rubric's test for high.
reasons.quote: Similar condition present in the prior year.

reasons.reason: The earlier audit in the window also had a serious finding on the same issue, which is a second, separate ground for high.
reasons.quote: did not include the Wage Rate (Davis Bacon Act) and DOL regulations.

reasons.reason: The auditor traced the 2024 problem to missing controls as well as oversight, so there is no case for lowering the rating as an isolated slip.
reasons.quote: due to oversight and a lack of controls in place

reasons.reason: The City filed its required audit form late for the second year running, a repeat finding that touches five federal awards.
reasons.quote: The City did not submit the data collection form for the year ended June 30, 2024 timely.

next_checks: Ask for evidence that the wage-rate (Davis-Bacon) terms are now in federally funded construction contracts. The 2024 response says procedures were put in place, but the audit data does not confirm it.

Check whether the 2025 audit has been issued and filed with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse, and whether it was on time. None is on file in the review window, and the form was late in both 2023 and 2024.

Get the financial-statement findings from the 2023 and 2024 audit reports. Both audits disclosed a financial-statement material weakness and material noncompliance, but the data here has no finding text explaining them.

sheet.summary: The City of Emporia rates high. Its latest audit (2024) has five findings, all marked as material weaknesses (the most serious kind of control failure), and one of them, late audit filing, repeats from the prior year. No text adjustment was made: the problems are not isolated or shown as corrected, and the rating is already at the top level.

reasons.reason: The late audit filing is marked as a material weakness and is a repeat from the prior year, which is what makes the rating high under step 2.
reasons.quote: This was a prior year finding. See Item 2023-001.

reasons.reason: The City is behind on its required audit filings, which the auditor says could put future federal funding at risk.
reasons.quote: The City has not met its single audit submission requirements.

reasons.reason: The City has no written purchasing rules beyond small purchases, a material weakness in how federal money is spent.
reasons.quote: The City does not maintain a procurement policy.

reasons.reason: Payments went out without City approval, and every payroll timesheet the auditor tested lacked it, a material weakness.
reasons.quote: We detected this through sampling in one out of seven disbursements tested and in six out of six payroll timesheets tested.

reasons.reason: A required federal recovery-fund report was filed late, a material weakness that the auditor links to staff changes.
reasons.quote: The delay in filing the report was due to transition of duties among the current staff.

reasons.reason: The City's list of federal spending was not checked before the audit and had to be changed, a material weakness.
reasons.quote: A review of the federal expenditures reported on the SEFA was not performed.

next_checks: The 2024 audit cites a prior-year finding 2023-001, but the data supplied here has no 2023 findings. Pull the 2023 audit and confirm what it reported.
No 2025 audit is on file in the review window. Confirm whether it has been submitted or when it is due, given the repeat late-filing finding.

Each finding points to a Corrective Action Plan that is not in this data. Obtain it and confirm whether the City has adopted a written procurement policy and now approves vendor payments and timesheets before paying.

sheet.summary: The 2025 audit found one serious problem: the City missed or was late with required federal spending reports for its Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. It is not a repeat finding, has no questioned costs, and the 2023 and 2024 audits had no findings, so the rating is medium. Management blames staff turnover, but the auditor ties the cause to this one program's reporting, so the rating was not moved up.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a finding the auditor marked as a material weakness (a serious control failure), which makes the rating medium under the rubric.
reasons.quote: During the fiscal year, the City had Project & Expenditure Reports which were either not submitted or were submitted more than 30 days after the end of the fiscal quarter.

reasons.reason: The auditor's stated cause is limited to reporting controls for this one program, so the text does not support moving the rating up as a systemic problem.
reasons.quote: The City did not have adequate controls in place to ensure that Project & Expenditure Reports were being filed in a timely manner.

reasons.reason: One quarterly report was never filed and another was over two months late, and nothing in the text shows this was fixed before the audit was issued, so the rating is not moved down.
reasons.quote: The Project & Expenditure Report for the first quarter of the fiscal year was required to be submitted by October 31, 2024, however no report was submitted.

next_checks: Confirm whether the missing first-quarter Project & Expenditure Report has since been filed and whether later quarterly reports were on time.

Management's response says heavy staff turnover drained institutional knowledge and that a CPA firm was engaged to help with internal controls. Ask the City whether that work was completed and what changed. If turnover is affecting other programs, consider whether a high rating is warranted.
The City was a low-risk auditee in 2023 and 2024 but not in 2025. Check whether reports on our own pass-through awards to the City have been late or missing.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: high. The 2025 audit has seven federal award findings, all tied to a modified opinion (the auditor could not give a clean compliance opinion for the program), and two of the most serious ones repeat from 2024. The auditor traces most of them to staff turnover and a missing grant accountant; the WIOA monitoring problem has now been reported three years running.

reasons.reason: The 2025 failure to monitor WIOA subrecipients was marked a material weakness (the most serious kind of control failure) and material noncompliance, which makes it a serious finding under the rubric.
reasons.quote: Subrecipient Monitoring – Material Noncompliance (Material Weakness)

reasons.reason: That same serious finding is a repeat of the prior year's finding, and a serious finding that repeats in the latest audit means a high rating.
reasons.quote: Repeat Finding 2024-002

reasons.reason: The same WIOA monitoring gap was reported in 2024, and that finding in turn was flagged as a repeat of 2023, so the problem has lasted the whole review window.
reasons.quote: There was a lack of evidence of testing and suggestions to the subrecipient during the fiscal year 2024.

reasons.reason: A second serious finding, on unreviewed Lead Hazard Control reports, also repeats from the prior year, which independently supports a high rating.
reasons.quote: Repeat Finding 2024-003

reasons.reason: The auditor gives the same staffing cause for the new serious findings on the COVID recovery funds, showing the problem is not limited to one program (context only; the rating is already at the top level, so no adjustment is made).
reasons.quote: Staff turnover, including the lack of a grant accountant.

reasons.reason: Reported spending on COVID recovery funds could not be matched to the City's own records, which weakens confidence in its federal financial reports.
reasons.quote: cumulative totals of expenditures did not agree to the total amounts reported on the

reasons.reason: Required federal financial reports for the Lead Hazard Control grant were not filed at all, a new material noncompliance in 2025.
reasons.quote: quarterly reports were not submitted.

next_checks: Ask the City whether a grant accountant has been hired, and request the monitoring schedule, checklist and completed desk reviews it says are now in place for WIOA and COVID recovery fund subrecipients.
Confirm the missing Lead Hazard Control SF-425 reports and the late CDBG PR29 report have been filed, and request evidence that a second person now reviews reports before submission.

Request the COVID recovery fund reconciliation the City says it completed; the response in finding 2025-007 dates it to the quarter ending June 30, 2026, which may be a typo for 2025. Also note the 2025 audit disclosed a material weakness and material noncompliance at the financial-statement level, and the City lost its low-risk auditee status that year.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: medium. The 2025 audit has three findings on federal awards, which meets the rubric's "three or more findings" test. None is serious (no material weakness or modified opinion), none is a repeat, none has questioned costs, and I made no adjustment from the text.

reasons.reason: This is one of three findings in the latest audit (2025), and three or more findings in the latest audit makes the rating medium.
reasons.quote: There was no evidence of review of two of the five reports tested.

reasons.reason: This is the second of the three 2025 findings: a supervisor's sign-off on an eligibility file was missing, though in one file only.
reasons.quote: In one instance, there was no evidence of supervisory approval on any forms.

reasons.reason: This is the third 2025 finding: the city did not give an organisation it passed federal money to all the required award details.
reasons.quote: All necessary information was not communicated to the subrecipient.

reasons.reason: The earlier audit (2024) also had a review-related finding, which does not change the rating but shows the same kind of gap the year before.
reasons.quote: The City’s review of the revenue loss calculation did not detect this error.

next_checks: Decide whether the review and documentation gaps across three programs in 2025 (Adoption Assistance, Coronavirus Recovery Funds, CDBG) plus the 2024 review finding amount to a systemic problem. I did not move the rating up because the auditor does not link them or trace them to the finance function as a whole.
Confirm the promised fixes are in place: documented review of CDBG reports from the quarter ended 9/30/2025, and preparer and supervisor sign-off on eligibility forms from fiscal year 2026.
Ask to see current subaward documents for the Coronavirus Recovery Funds to confirm they now carry the federal award number, program listing number and awarding agency name.

sheet.summary: Bedford County's latest audit (2025) and its 2024 audit have no findings on federal awards. The only finding in the window is from 2023: the County filed its 2022 audit report form late with the federal clearinghouse, and the auditor marked this as a repeat finding. No audit in the window disclosed a financial-statement material weakness, material noncompliance or a going-concern doubt.

reasons.reason: The only finding in the review window is in an earlier audit (2023), not the latest one, and it is not a serious finding and has no questioned costs, which fits the rubric's low rating.
reasons.quote: The County did not file the data collection form for the year ended June 30, 2022 timely.

reasons.reason: I considered moving the rating up one level because the finding covers 13 awards and mentions staff turnover, but did not, because the turnover is cited in management's response rather than by the auditor and the finding is about one late filing, not weak controls over the programs.
reasons.quote: was due to the 2022 audit being completed late because of significant staff turnover.

reasons.reason: Management's response says it acted on the staffing cause, and the 2024 and 2025 audits have no findings, which supports leaving the rating at low.
reasons.quote: has since filled vacant positions, added one position, and restructured the department to help with

next_checks: Confirm the 2024 and 2025 audit report forms were filed with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse on time; the absence of findings in those years suggests so, but the data does not give filing dates.
The 2023 finding was marked as a repeat, so check the 2022 audit (outside this window) to see how long the late filing had been going on.
Ask the County whether the finance positions it says it filled after the 2022 turnover are still filled.

sheet.summary: Medium risk. The latest audit on file (2024) has one finding, and it repeats the 2023 finding: the County has no written purchasing rules of its own that meet federal grant standards. The auditor did not mark it as a material weakness (the most serious kind of control problem) and questioned no costs, and there is no 2025 audit on file.

reasons.reason: The latest audit's only finding is marked as a repeat finding, which makes the rating medium under the rubric.
reasons.quote: The County does not have its own written procurement policies that conform to applicable Federal laws and regulations and standards.

reasons.reason: The same gap was first reported the year before, so it has now gone uncorrected through two audits.
reasons.quote: the County does not have complete, written procurement

reasons.reason: The fix was still under way when the 2024 audit was issued, so the text does not support moving the rating down, and nothing in it shows a wider finance-function problem that would move it up.
reasons.quote: Management concurs and has begun updating existing written procurement procedures

next_checks: Ask the County for its updated written procurement policy and confirm it has been adopted and covers the federal standards in 2 CFR 200.317 to 200.326.
Confirm which two federal awards the 2024 finding affects; the data flags two, but the finding text names only the Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (AL# 21.027).
Check whether a 2025 audit has been filed and, if so, whether this finding appears a third time.

sheet.summary: The 2025 audit has three findings on federal awards, two of them serious, all touching the Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Fund. None is a repeat or is flagged with questioned costs, and 2023 and 2024 have no federal award findings on file, so the rubric gives medium, not high. All three audits also disclosed a material weakness in the financial statements, with no finding text to explain it.

reasons.reason: The auditor marked this 2025 finding as a material weakness, which makes it a serious finding in the latest audit: the county's schedule of federal spending left out grant spending.
reasons.quote: The SEFA was understated by $175,000 for the E&T LE Grant.

reasons.reason: This 2025 finding led to a modified opinion on compliance for the program, so it is a second serious finding in the latest audit.
reasons.quote: No supporting documentation for key line items on P&E expenditure report.

reasons.reason: This is the third finding in the latest audit, which on its own meets the medium test of three or more findings; it covers both the recovery fund and the child nutrition programs.
reasons.quote: The County does not have a Uniform Guidance Procurement Manual.

reasons.reason: The data flag says this finding has no questioned costs, so the rating stays medium, but the finding text gives an amount under a questioned-cost heading; if the flag is wrong, the rubric would give high.
reasons.quote: P&E report was understated by $186,000.

next_checks: Check finding 2025-017 in the source audit: the text shows a "Questioned Cost Amount" of $186,000 but the questioned-costs flag is No. If questioned costs do apply, the rating becomes high.

Decide whether to move the rating up one level for a systemic problem. I did not, but finding 2025-016 (no procurement manual) spans two programs, and the 2023, 2024 and 2025 audits each disclosed a financial-statement material weakness with no finding text in this data.

Confirm the county has done what it promised: a procurement manual for all departments, a verified recovery-fund spending spreadsheet, and a schedule of federal spending checked against a full list of expenditures.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: low. The latest audit (2025) has one finding, late Medicaid eligibility reviews, and the auditor did not flag it as serious, repeated or carrying questioned costs. The 2025 audit is also marked as disclosing material noncompliance (a significant rule breach), which the finding text does not explain, so a reviewer should look at this before approving.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has only this one finding, and it is not flagged as serious, repeated or carrying questioned costs, which fits a low rating under the rubric.
reasons.quote: In 4 of the 25 cases tested, eligibility redetermination had not been completed

reasons.reason: The auditor's text does not show the problem was already corrected before the audit was issued, so the rating is not moved down, and it describes one program only, so it is not moved up.
reasons.quote: The agency will implement procedures to improve timeliness.

reasons.reason: This earlier finding was serious because it led to a modified opinion on compliance for a federal program, but it does not raise the rating because the latest audit has no serious finding.
reasons.quote: The Workforce Development Board has not had a current audit in accordance with Uniform Guidance.

next_checks: The 2025 audit is marked as disclosing material noncompliance, but finding 2025-001 is not marked as a material weakness or a modified opinion. Check the 2025 audit report to see what the flag refers to and whether the finding should count as serious, which would change the rating.
Confirm the West Piedmont Workforce Development Board has since obtained its required audit. The 2024 and 2025 data show no repeat of finding 2023-001 but do not say it was resolved.
Ask the local social services agency for the current number of overdue Medicaid eligibility redeterminations and the procedures it put in place to improve timeliness.

sheet.summary: Low, because the only federal award finding in the window is from 2023, and the 2024 and 2025 audits have none. That 2023 finding was a repeat finding about a required report, but it was not a material weakness and had no questioned costs. Separately, all three audits disclosed a material weakness (a serious gap in financial controls) in the county's financial statements, and the data has no text explaining it.

reasons.reason: The only federal award finding in the window is this 2023 reporting finding, and with none in the latest audit (2025) the rubric gives a low rating.
reasons.quote: a Project and Expenditure Report (P&E) was due by April 30, 2023 and annually thereafter.

next_checks: Read the 2023, 2024 and 2025 audit reports to find out what the financial-statement material weakness is each year; the data flags it but gives no text.
Read the full text of finding 2023-004 to see what went wrong with the Project and Expenditure Report; the text here states only the due date, and the finding is marked as a repeat.
Confirm in the 2024 and 2025 reports that finding 2023-004 was resolved and that there are no federal award findings in those years.

sheet.summary: The latest audit (2025) has no findings on federal awards, and the only finding in the window is a 2024 school meals over-claim, so the rubric gives a low rating. That low rating is not a clean bill of health. The 2025 and 2024 audits both disclosed a material weakness (a serious gap in financial controls) and material noncompliance at the financial-statement level, with no finding text in the data to explain them.

reasons.reason: The only federal award finding in the window is from 2024, an earlier audit, and it carries questioned costs, which would count toward a higher rating only if it were in the latest audit.
reasons.quote: There are likely questioned costs of $124,430 (consisting of $24,886 in known questioned costs) related to over claiming school nutrition reimbursements.

reasons.reason: The auditor traces the problem to data entry mistakes in one program, not to a breakdown across the finance function, so the text does not support moving the rating up.
reasons.quote: Reimbursements require manual data entry and amounts were requested in error.

reasons.reason: The fix was a promise at the time of the audit, not something already done, so the text does not support moving the rating down either.
reasons.quote: The School Board will implement a review process to ensure the manually entered meal counts agree to the supporting documentation.

next_checks: Get the 2025 audit report and read what lies behind the material weakness and material noncompliance it disclosed. The data has no finding text for them, and the county was not a low-risk auditee in 2025.
Confirm the School Board put the meal count review in place, and that the 2025 audit did not repeat finding 2024-005.
Ask whether the Virginia Department of Education has resolved the questioned costs ($24,886 known, $124,430 likely) and whether any money was repaid.

sheet.summary: Low risk under the rubric. The latest audit (2025) has one finding: the school system could not show that someone other than the preparer reviewed three monthly reimbursement requests. It was not a serious finding, not a repeat, and had no questioned costs; the only other finding in the window (2023) was a similar-sized records gap at the schools.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a single finding, about missing proof of independent review on three of the reimbursement requests tested, which the auditor classed as a significant deficiency (a lesser control weakness, not a material weakness).
reasons.quote: For three of the monthly reimbursement requests selected for testing

reasons.reason: The auditor questioned no costs on the 2025 finding, so it does not trigger a medium rating.
reasons.quote: There are no questioned costs related to this finding

reasons.reason: The auditor marked the 2025 finding as not a repeat, so it does not trigger a medium rating.
reasons.quote: Repeat Finding: No

reasons.reason: The only earlier finding in the window was also a lesser weakness with no questioned costs, about one missing vendor check, so there is no history of serious findings.
reasons.quote: The suspension and debarment status for one out of two vendors was not retained

reasons.reason: No adjustment was made: the auditor ties the 2025 cause to record-keeping for reimbursement reports at the school system, not to the wider finance function, and the text does not say it was fixed before the audit was issued.
reasons.quote: evidence of review and approval of the reimbursement reports.

next_checks: Ask the school system for evidence that monthly reimbursement requests are now reviewed and signed off by someone other than the preparer; the 2025 finding does not say this has been fixed.
Identify which three federal awards finding 2025-001 affects, since the finding text does not name them, and confirm whether any are passed through by this office.
The 2023 audit and finding 2023-001 each appear twice in the data with identical content; confirm this is a duplicate record and not a second finding.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: low, because the only federal award finding in the window is from 2023 and the latest audit (2025) has none. That 2023 finding was serious, though: a material weakness (the worst grade of control failure), a repeat, with questioned costs and a modified opinion on compliance. All three audits, including 2025, also disclosed a material weakness in the financial statements, which comes with no finding text here.

reasons.reason: This is the only federal award finding in the window and it sits in an earlier audit (2023), not the latest one (2025), which the rubric rates as low.
reasons.quote: Program Titles: Education Stabilization Fund

next_checks: Read the full text of finding 2023-003 in the 2023 audit report. The data here gives only the program title, so there was no text to judge whether the rating should move up or down a level.

Confirm that the 2024 and 2025 audits really had no federal award findings, and that the 2023 questioned costs on the Education Stabilization Fund were resolved. 2023-003 was flagged as a repeat finding and as affecting 4 federal awards.

Look up the financial-statement material weakness disclosed in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025. It does not count toward the rubric rating, but it recurs every year and may point to a wider finance problem.

sheet.summary: High risk. The latest audit (2024) found that the transit company again paid contractors and vendors late on its federal transit grants. The auditor marked this as a material weakness (the most serious kind of control failure) and as a repeat of the 2023 finding. No 2025 audit is on file, and no questioned costs or going-concern doubt were reported.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a serious finding (a material weakness that also led to a modified compliance opinion) which the auditor flagged as a repeat, and the rubric rates that high.
reasons.quote: We noted 14 instances where contractors and vendors were not paid for over 30 days. We also noted four vendors were not paid for over 90 days.

reasons.reason: The earlier audit in the window also had a serious finding on the same late-payment problem, which is a second, separate ground for a high rating.
reasons.quote: Lack of proactive cash flow and grant management occurred when invoices were received.

reasons.reason: The latest audit also found expired grants left open with money still on them, and the auditor gave the same cause as for the late payments, so the problem is not isolated.
reasons.quote: All 6 were still marked as active in the grant award management system as of June 30, 2024, with total remaining funds on these awards totaling $673,179.

reasons.reason: A third finding in the latest audit, on missing required federal contract clauses, adds to the count but is minor and does not change the rating.
reasons.quote: did not contain these clauses in one contract tested

next_checks: Confirm whether a 2025 audit has been filed. None is in the data, so this rating rests on the 2024 audit.
Ask for evidence that vendors are now paid on time and grant draws are made promptly, including the Monthly Close Checklist and grant tracking spreadsheets that management said it was developing.
Check the closeout status of the six expired federal grants and what happened to the $673,179 left on them.

sheet.summary: Lee County's latest audit (2025) has no findings on federal awards, and the only finding in the window is from 2023, so the rubric gives a low rating. That 2023 finding was serious: a repeat problem with questioned costs, where the County did not check a subrecipient's requests for Department of Labor money. Low is not a clean bill of health: all three audits, including 2025, disclosed a material weakness and material noncompliance in the financial statements, with no finding text on file to explain them.

reasons.reason: The only finding in the window is from 2023, an earlier audit, so under the rubric it supports a low rating even though it was a serious repeat finding with questioned costs.
reasons.quote: Funds are requested for drawdown by the subrecipient without the County reviewing

reasons.reason: The auditor put the problem down to a misunderstanding of one requirement, not to missing staff or absent controls across the finance function, so the text does not justify moving the rating up.
reasons.quote: The County misunderstood the compliance requirements for subrecipient monitoring.

reasons.reason: The County only promised a future fix, so the text does not show the problem was corrected before the audit was issued and gives no ground to change the rating.
reasons.quote: The County will work with the subrecipient to implement necessary controls to be in compliance.

next_checks: Get the 2024 and 2025 audit reports and read what the disclosed material weakness and material noncompliance were; the data here flags them but has no finding text.
Confirm that the 2024 and 2025 audits really have no federal award findings, and that finding 2023-007 (already a repeat in 2023) was closed and not just left out of the data.
Find the dollar amount of the questioned costs in finding 2023-007 and whether they were resolved; the finding text gives no amount.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: high. The 2024 audit, the only one on file for 2023 to 2025, has three findings that the auditor marked as material weaknesses (the most serious kind of control failure), which gives medium under the rubric. I moved it up one level because the auditor traces all three to finance staff turnover and missing controls across the accounting function.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a finding marked as a material weakness, which is a serious finding and sets the starting rating at medium.
reasons.quote: The Commission is not timely reconciling the bank accounts.

reasons.reason: A second material weakness shows the Commission could not reliably report how much federal money it spent on each award.
reasons.quote: The Commission did not have sufficient controls to ensure the SEFA accurately reflected each award’s federal expenditures.

reasons.reason: A third material weakness shows the audit itself was filed late, and brings the latest audit to three findings.
reasons.quote: The Commission did not submit the single audit reporting package to the Federal Audit Clearinghouse within nine months after the end of the audit period as required.

reasons.reason: Adjustment up one level, from medium to high: the auditor traces the problem to missing staff and absent controls across the finance function, which the rubric treats as systemic.
reasons.quote: The Commission had staff turnover in the finance position and did not have sufficient controls and redundancies to allow all accounting functions to be performed on a timely basis.

reasons.reason: Supports the upward adjustment: the missing bank reconciliations led to many errors in the books that the auditor had to correct.
reasons.quote: resulted in numerous audit adjustments to correct posting errors

next_checks: Confirm whether the promised fixes are in place: the written policies on monthly bank reconciliations, revenue recording and the audit timeline, the cross-training of staff, and whether the finance position is now filled.
Find out why no 2023 or 2025 audit is on file in the review window, and whether the 2025 audit is late.

The 2024 audit record is flagged for a financial-statement material weakness and material noncompliance, and the Commission is not a low-risk auditee. Read the full audit report to see what the material noncompliance refers to, because the finding text does not say.

sheet.summary: The 2024 audit (the latest on file) has two findings, both for late filing and neither marked serious, which is a low rating on the flags alone. I moved it up one level to medium because the auditor traces both to vacant finance department posts, including the Senior Finance Director, and the lateness touches more than one federal program. Separately, the 2024 audit disclosed a material weakness (a serious control gap) in the financial statements, with no finding text in the data to explain it.

reasons.reason: The year-end performance report to the state for the Mental Health Block Grant was filed about six weeks after the extended deadline; this is one of only two findings, neither serious, repeated nor with questioned costs, so the flags alone give low.
reasons.quote: The Agency filed its end of year performance contract report with the DBHDS on October 30, 2024.

reasons.reason: The audit itself was not finished by the federal filing deadline, the second late-filing finding in the latest audit.
reasons.quote: The Agency’s audit was not yet completed at March 31, 2025.

reasons.reason: Adjustment up one level, from low to medium: the auditor traces the late filings to missing finance staff, which the rubric treats as a sign of a systemic problem.
reasons.quote: The Agency had two vacant positions in the Finance Department

reasons.reason: Supporting the same upward adjustment: the late audit filing affects more than one federal program, not a single grant.
reasons.quote: Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds ALN 21.027 and Mental Health Block Grant

next_checks: Get the 2024 audit report and read what the financial-statement material weakness was; the data flags it but gives no text.
Ask whether the two finance vacancies, including the Senior Finance Director, are now filled and whether the data problems with the new software system are resolved.
No 2025 audit is on file in the review window; check whether it is due or overdue and whether the performance contract report was filed on time this year.

546001452.name: Newport News Redevelopment and Housing Authority

sheet.summary: The 2025 audit found two major, repeated compliance failures in the housing voucher program, one of them with costs the auditor questioned. The 2024 audit found major failures in the same areas. No text-based adjustment was made: the problems are not isolated or corrected, and high is already the top rating.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a serious finding (a material weakness with a modified opinion on compliance) on rent checks that the auditor marks as a repeat of 2024-005, which meets the high test.
reasons.quote: 24 out of 120 files tested did not have a rent reasonableness determination form completed before the rent effective date.

reasons.reason: A second serious finding in the latest audit, on housing inspections, is also a repeat and shows a large share of the 65 units tested were not inspected on time.
reasons.quote: 27 units did not have inspections performed on a biennial basis
